sentences.text: It is submitted by the learned counsel on behalf of appellants that the issue of compensation for the land acquisition for construction of canal of Bhairwa Jalashaya, had been settled in another set of cases of which judgment was delivered on 28.01.2011 (Annexure-A) and by the same Court, the Land Reference Case No.178-207 of 2009 has been dismissed by the impugned order dated 22.12.2011.

Reliance is placed on Jaipur Development Authority Versus Kailashwati Devi (Smt.), (1997) 7 SCC 297, Sharda (Smt) & Others Versus Manikkoth Kombra Rajendran, (1996) 8 SCC 345, Satish Chand Surana Versus Raj Kumar Meshram (Civil Appeal No.7446 of 2021).
Learned counsel on behalf of State has contested the petition for additional evidence and a counter affidavit has been filed to the Interlocutory Applications.

sentences.text: It is submitted that the appellants had sufficient opportunity during the pendency before the learned Land Acquisition Court to adduce the evidence which was not availed and the instant petitions under Order XLI, Rule 27 of the C.P.C. has been filed at the belated stage.

It is argued that the judgment which the appellants seek to adduce into evidence before this Court, was very much available with these appellants as it was delivered about one year before the judgment which has been impugned in the present case.
Despite this, the said judgment was not filed before the learned trial Court.

Matter for consideration is whether the Judgment which the Appellants seek to adduced into evidence, is relevant for hearing of the First Appeals and if it meets the statutory mandate to adduce additional evidence at this stage?
In order to appreciate the law on the point it shall be desirable to extract the relevant provision of Order XLI Rule.27 which is as under:-
Production of additional evidence in Appellate Court-- The party in appeal is entitled to produce additional evidence whether oral or documentary in the following circumstances:
1. The Court from whom the appeal is preferred has improperly refused to admit evidence 2.

The party seeking to adduce additional evidence establishes that notwithstanding the exercise of due diligence, the evidence was not within his knowledge or it could not be produced by him at the time when the decree appealed against was passed.
3. The appellate court requires any document to be produced or witness to be examined to enable it to pronounce Judgment, or for any other substantial cause 4.
Wherever additional evidence is allowed the court shall record reason for its admission.

The discretion for allowing additional evidence cannot be allowed for introducing new pleas at the appellate stage.
Additional evidence cannot be allowed when the party had sufficient opportunity at the trial stage.
Union of India v. Ibrahim Uddin, (2012) 8 SCC 148 "The general principle is that the appellate court should not travel outside the record of the lower court and cannot take any evidence in appeal.

entities.text: Union of India v. Ibrahim Uddin, (2012) 8 SCC 148
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, as an exception, Order 41 Rule 27 CPC enables the appellate court to take additional evidence in exceptional circumstances.
The appellate court may permit additional evidence only and only if the conditions laid down in this Rule are found to exist.
The parties are not entitled, as of right, to the admission of such evidence.
Thus, the provision does not apply, when on the basis of the evidence on record, the appellate court can pronounce a satisfactory judgment.
The matter is entirely within the discretion of the court and is to be used sparingly.
Such a discretion is only a judicial discretion circumscribed by the limitation specified in the Rule itself."

In the present case, the document that the appellant seeks to adduce into evidence is a judgment delivered in another case, which cannot be relevant for the reason that all judgments except those under Sections 40 and 41 of the Evidence Act decides right in personam and cannot be said to be relevant in another case where the facts may be different.
Compensation is decided on the basis of evidence adduced before the Court with respect to the land acquired.
Different factors come into play in computing the compensation which includes the nature of land, whether it was a commercial or agricultural or urban land.
Every plot of land has a different topography and nature.

Therefore,
any compensation awarded in another case cannot be treated as a yardstick for determination of compensation in any other case.

This Court is of the view that the judgment sought to be adduced as additional evidence is not relevant for consideration in the present appeal, nor the appellant has succeeded to give plausible explanation for not reducing the same before the learned Court below.
The interlocutory applications do not merit consideration and are accordingly rejected.
Let these cases be listed on 19.04.2024.
